messages:
jia: Noticing a cluster of reports from a few customers about stalled SSE streams that reconnect and sometimes show duplicate token usage. Spike started right after last proxy roll.
kevin: region? any pattern across routes (ws vs sse)?
jia: Primarily us-east and us-west edge. Both SSE and WS clients affected but hits are higher on long-lived SSE sessions.
ops-bot: [ALERT] StreamReconnects(us-east) > baseline at 1762223338
maria: I pulled traces. Theres a pattern where proxy returns 204 (no-body) to client to indicate "please resubscribe" while upstream concurrently accepts a resume and emits billing. Client then resubscribes from start token. That results in duplicated billed tokens.
raghav: so ordering bug: billing event emitted before proxy fence/reject is visible to client? any logs?
jia: snippets:
```
[12:02:12] proxy-2 resume_request id=rid-9a session=shard-3 -> forwarded
[12:02:12] billing-emitter stream_resume id=rid-9a tokens=120
[12:02:12] proxy-2 respond 204 session=shard-3 fence=1
[12:02:13] client reconnect -> resubscribe from earlier offset
```
kevin: ugh. The billing path probably receives a "resume accepted" event from upstream before we atomically check the fence flag. Two fixes: make billing emission come after fence check OR make resume idempotent at billing layer.
sasha: From console UX side we don't expose resume-level failures; customers just see cost spikes. We should add a per-connection timeline on the route detail page with: resume_attempts, fence_events, billing_events, and a simple "duplicate token" rate.
maria: short term mitigation: configure proxy to delay 204 responses by 1s on canary to allow resume flow to settle. Not ideal but buys time.
kevin: I'll put up a proxy config PR for a canary with delayed 204 for 5% us-east/us-west. Also adding a feature flag to toggle delay.
raghav: mid-term: server should attach a resume_handled boolean to billing-emitter and billing should check resume_idempotency table (TTL 15m). That prevents double-bill even if upstream races. I'll prototype.
ops-bot: [DEPLOY] Starting proxy-canary delayed-204 (5%) at 1762223460
jia: Can we also add a new metric: streaming.resume_outcome with tags {route, resume_id, charge} and expose it in Grafana? We need to alert if charge=true and client_reconnect_with_resubscribe=true within 2s.
sasha: Will add dashboard card: "Resume integrity" under streaming -> health. Will include sparkline and a log link that pre-fills resume_id. Ticket DASH-1007.
kevin: Canary live. Monitoring: duplicate_token_rate in canary shard dropped from 0.6% -> 0.08% within 3m.
ops-bot: [DEPLOY] Canary healthy at 1762223520 :white_check_mark:
maria: Opening server PR for idempotency table: https://git/redwood/streaming/+/801. It emits resume_idempotency_event so console can correlate.
raghav: I'll coordinate with billing infra to add a guard in emitter that checks recent resume_ids before emitting charge.
jia: Good. After we verify server fix in canary for 30m, plan to remove delayed-204 and roll the idempotency change. Also add post-deploy test that replays resume race scenario.
kevin: Filed proxy config change PR: https://git/redwood/proxy/+/222
sasha: Dashboard ticket: DASH-1007 created. Will prototype a compact timeline widget.
ops-bot: [NOTES] Incident tracker created: STREAM-INC-2026
jia: Thanks all. Keep watch for regressions and postmortem notes if we still see user-facing billing duplicates.
kevin: I'll increase canary to 20% in 40m if metrics stay steady.
maria: Adding an alert rule: streaming.duplicate_token_rate > 0.1% for 5m -> page oncall. Ticket STREAM-4570.
raghav: I'll add an integration test that simulates concurrent resume+fence to avoid regressions.
jia: closing loop: we'll update runbook with the delayed-204 mitigation and the idempotency rollback steps.
